Alliteration Marker

Paste a poem and the tool matches each word's sounds to its letters, using British pronunciations (American ones, converted, fill any gaps; the dictionary is built into this file, so it works offline). You choose what to mark: left-click a sound to mark it, right-click to change it.

Sound chart

1 · Paste the poem

Bold letters mark stressed syllables. Multi-syllable words keep their dictionary stress; the meter decides which one-syllable words (and secondary-stress syllables) count as stressed. Each stanza can override this in step 2. Once you have started marking, change the text with Edit poem text in step 2 (re-pasting here starts over).

2 · Mark the sounds

Left-click a sound to mark it; click again to unmark. Hover first to see which letters a click will mark. Right-click (or long-press) for options: change the sound, adjust which letters it covers, or choose another pronunciation of the word. Right-click letters with no sound, such as a silent e, to give them one. Words underlined with dots were guessed from their spelling. Stressed syllables are bold (set by the meter and the dictionary). Turn Edit stress on, then click a syllable to stress or un-stress it, or drag across exact letters; or right-click a syllable. Turn Italics on and drag across letters or words you want to note; right-click italic letters to remove it, or drag across them again. Show only hides every mark outside the groups you pick (groups can be combined); hidden sounds are not clickable until you show them again. Save work downloads a small file with the poem, your marks, stress edits, and sound corrections; reopen it later with Open saved work at the top of this page.

Phonetic Markup for Verse: created by Eric J. Kingsepp (Éadric Scúsmiþ), 2026.

Pronunciations: British English from ipa-dict (en_UK, MIT license), whose data derives from ipacards by @leoboiko (GPL-3.0); American English from the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (© 1993–2015 Carnegie Mellon University), converted to British-style sounds by rule. Matching sounds to letters is done by this tool and can be wrong: right-click to correct it.

Edit poem text

Change words or line breaks. Marks, stress edits and italics stay on every word you leave alone, and on lightly retyped words (typo fixes) wherever the sound is unchanged. New or rewritten words are matched fresh.
